payload.task_text:
I am writing a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning methods for my research group. Please look up the chain-of-thought reasoning papers in the arxiv-latex database and help me organize the findings. The database holds several papers, but only five are about chain-of-thought reasoning methods; the others are about word representations and are out of scope. The five reasoning papers, by arXiv ID, are: 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, and 2305.10601. Use the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract) with these IDs to retrieve each paper's title and abstract.

Create a Google Sheet called "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with a sheet named "Papers" that lists the reasoning-related papers. The columns should be Title, Year, Method, and Key_Contribution. For the Method column, try to identify the main reasoning approach described in each paper (for example "chain-of-thought prompting", "self-consistency", "zero-shot CoT", "automatic CoT", or "tree of thoughts"). For Key_Contribution, write a brief one-sentence description of the paper's main contribution. Only include papers that are about reasoning methods, not papers about word embeddings or word representations.

Also create a Word document called "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in my workspace. The document should have the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at the top, followed by today's date (2026-03-06). Then include a section for each reasoning paper, mentioning its title and briefly describing its contribution. End with a short conclusion paragraph.

Note: this task has two deliverables — the Google Sheet and the Word document. If you are running as a team of agents, divide the work between agents (for example, assign the spreadsheet to one agent and the Word document to another) or otherwise serialize your writes, so that both deliverables are completed without conflicting writes to the same file.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself retrieves the five fixed papers' title and abstract (five light read-only calls, no research wave), freezes one canonical five-row packet, and dispatches exactly one parallel writer wave of two independent deliverable owners.

Before the wave, the main agent resolves the runtime workspace, freezes the five explicit arXiv IDs — 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, 2305.10601 — and today's required displayed date 2026-03-06. It calls the arxiv-latex abstract/prompt retrieval once per ID, extracts title/year/method label/key contribution from the returned abstracts only, excludes all word-representation material, and freezes five literal rows {arxiv_id, title, year, method, key_contribution} plus per-ID retrieval controls.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): The Google Sheet writer: create a spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with exactly one sheet named "Papers" (rename the default sheet or create the named one), write the header row Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution followed by exactly the five frozen rows, then read the complete range back and return the spreadsheet/sheet IDs, header check and row count. Do not create the Word document.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): The Word writer: create Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx in the resolved workspace with the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison", the literal date 2026-03-06, one section per frozen paper mentioning its title and contribution, and a short conclusion paragraph, then read the document outline and text back. Do not create the spreadsheet.

The two writers serialize only through their own distinct files and never touch each other's deliverable. After the wave, the main agent reconciles both read-backs against the frozen packet (five rows/sections each, exact title/date, reasoning-only scope) and calls claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

nodes.text:
I need precise bibliographic info for five arXiv papers about chain-of-thought reasoning. For each of the following arXiv IDs, use the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract) to determine the paper's EXACT title and the year it was published (use the year implied by the arXiv ID's YYMM prefix, e.g. a 22xx ID is 2022).

The five IDs are:
- 2201.11903
- 2203.11171
- 2205.11916
- 2210.03493
- 2305.10601

For each paper, return a compact structured list with: arxiv_id, exact_title, year. Do not write to any file. Just return the five entries in your final message. I already have the abstracts, so I only need the exact titles and years.
Confirm paper titles and years

Create a Word document and write all content into it. The workspace directory for all files is:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace

Use the mcp__word__ tools. Create a NEW document at the absolute path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx

The document must contain the following content, in order:

1. A top-level title (Heading/Title style) with the text: "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison"

2. A line with the date: "Date: 2026-03-06"

3. Then ONE section (heading) for each of the following five papers. Use a heading for each (e.g., "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (2022)") followed by a short paragraph briefly describing the paper's contribution. Use these exact facts:

   - Paper: "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models" (2022). Contribution: This paper introduces chain-of-thought prompting, showing that generating a series of intermediate reasoning steps significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks.

   - Paper: "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models" (2022). Contribution: This paper introduces self-consistency, a decoding strategy that replaces naive greedy decoding by sampling a diverse set of reasoning paths and then selecting the most consistent answer by marginalizing over the sampled paths.

   - Paper: "Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners" (2022). Contribution: This paper shows that simply adding the phrase "Let's think step by step" before each answer significantly enables zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models, without any hand-crafted demonstrations.

   - Paper: "Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models" (2022). Contribution: This paper proposes Auto-CoT, which automatically constructs demonstrations with questions and reasoning chains using clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, removing the need for manually written exemplars.

   - Paper: "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models" (2023). Contribution: This paper introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, which generalizes chain-of-thought prompting by enabling exploration over coherent units of text (thoughts) and supports deliberate search and backtracking for complex problem solving.

4. Finally, end with a heading "Conclusion" and a short conclusion paragraph. Suggested conclusion text (write your own phrasing if preferred, keeping roughly this meaning): "In summary, chain-of-thought prompting established that eliciting intermediate reasoning steps unlocks complex reasoning in large language models. Subsequent work improved upon it along three axes: more reliable decoding via self-consistency, more accessible prompting via zero-shot and automatic chain-of-thought, and more deliberate search via tree of thoughts. Together these methods form a coherent progression from reasoning-by-demonstration toward more robust and exploratory reasoning, and they remain a foundation for current research on structured reasoning in language models."

Use mcp__word__create_document first, then mcp__word__add_heading and mcp__word__add_paragraph as needed. Do not create any other files. The only deliverable is the .docx file at the path above. When done, confirm the file exists by listing the document or getting its text, and report the final file path.
